label: Long Voyage test: the phone game on the board, BLE sync (game firmware)
notes: Test build for the bench, not a stable release; nothing updates to it on its own. Needs the game firmware first: flash lv-core-0.1.0-f1b383588e79-RPI_PICO_W.uf2 by hand (hold BOOTSEL, drop the file on the RPI-RP2 drive); this page refuses to install on any other firmware. Then set the ship number in section 4, the crew codes and the launch date (flight day 1 starts at 06:00 that day and a new flight day every morning at 06:00, 42 days; leave it blank for the manual bench day), install, and power-cycle. Join the LV-<ship number> hotspot with a phone: the game opens by itself (or browse to any http address) and every crew member signs in with their code. BLE sync between ships keeps running. New in this build: the phone talks to you in the second person. Your own astronaut is "you" everywhere on your phone (the log, the plan sheet, gifts, cargo, watch duty, the briefing, the crew file and the ending) and everyone else keeps their name; the daily instruction is now your plan. Also: a fuller first-run briefing (the goal, how ships, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth work, why to come back each day, gifts and the ship light), and the crew list and gift pickers show which ships are in Bluetooth range now and when each was last heard. Optional ship battery: a UPS-Lite v1.3 wired to the Pico W (game/docs/BATTERY.md) is found by itself, and the phones show its charge at the top of the page; boards without one are unchanged. The ship light: With "Pulse the onboard light" ticked (or Ship light on the phone's own crew page), the Pico W's LED now breathes instead of blinking: one slow breath every few seconds while today's page waits, a double pulse for a gift, three quick breaths for a new flight day; dark 22:00-07:00 and once a phone has looked. The bench LED test (--led-test) plays 3 slow breaths and asks if you saw it pulse. Faster bench: from the repo, python3 game/tools/bench.py --ship N installs this build over USB, runs the self-test and prints a PASS/FAIL report (docs/BENCH_TEST.md). Check from the REPL with: import selftest; selftest.run(120). Your settings in data/ are kept. To go back, install 0.0.2-coex (it runs on the game firmware too). Sealed board: main.py waits 2 s after power-up before touching the radio, so any mpremote command (Ctrl-C) in that window gets the REPL; an empty data/safe skips the game on every boot.
